header.title: How To Make Your Own Battery
header.description: This guide demonstrates how to create a simple battery using common household materials through two different methods: one using a plastic cup, water, and metal strips, and another using a soda can and aluminum.

steps.description: Step 1 - Fill a Plastic Cup with Water
actions: Fill a plastic cup three quarters of the way full with tap water. The cup for this doesn’t have to be plastic, but it must be non-metallic. A paper or foam cup would also work.

steps.description: Add a tablespoon of salt to the water and stir it well.
actions: Add a tablespoon of salt
Stir it well

steps.description: Place two metal strips, one of zinc, aluminum, or copper, on opposite sides of the cup, ensuring the bottom of each strip touches the salt water and the top is folded over the rim.
actions: Obtain two metal strips of different metals (zinc, aluminum, or copper).
Place one strip on each side of the cup.
Ensure the bottom of each strip is touching the salt water.
Fold the other end of each strip slightly over the rim.

steps.description: Attach lead wires to the metal strips using alligator clips, ensuring the clips don't touch the water.
actions: Attach a lead wire to one of the metal strips using an alligator clip.
Attach a different lead wire to the other strip, also using an alligator clip.
Don’t let the alligator clips touch the water.

steps.description: Connect lead wires to a voltage meter to test the battery's strength.
actions: Connect the other ends of your lead wires to a voltage meter
Test the strength of your battery

steps.description: Fill a plastic cup with soda until it's about three-quarters full.
actions: Using a plastic cup
Fill it with soda
Until it’s approximately three-quarters of the way full

steps.description: Completely empty the can by discarding or consuming the excess soda.
actions: Discard the excess soda
Drink the excess soda
Empty the can

steps.description: Cut a strip of aluminum from the soda can, ensuring it's the correct width and length.
actions: Cut a strip of aluminum
Make the strip three-quarters or an inch wide
Make the strip slightly longer than the height of the cup

steps.description: Sand the coating off the sides of the aluminum strip.
actions: Sand off the coating

steps.description: Place aluminum and copper strips into the soda, ensuring they don't touch each other and hang over the rim.
actions: Place the aluminum strip into the soda
Place a copper strip into the soda across from the aluminum strip
Ensure each strip is touching the soda
Ensure each strip is hanging over the top of the rim
Don’t allow the strips to touch each other

steps.description: Connect lead wires to the aluminum and copper strips using alligator clips, ensuring the clips don't touch the soda.
actions: Attach a lead wire to the aluminum strip
Connect the lead wire to the aluminum strip with an alligator clip
Attach a lead wire to the copper strip
Connect the lead wire to the copper strip with an alligator clip
Do not let the alligator clips touch the soda

steps.description: Use a voltage meter to check the battery's strength by connecting lead wires to it.
actions: Attach the lead wires from each strip to a voltage meter
Read the voltage meter

steps.description: Place an aluminum and copper plate on a non-metallic surface like wood or plastic.
actions: Place an aluminum plate
Place a copper plate
Place plates next to each other
Place plates on a piece of wood (optional)
Place plates on a non-metallic surface (alternative)

steps.description: Connect the sheets to a voltage meter using alligator clips.
actions: Use alligator clips
Connect sheets to a voltage meter

steps.description: Place your hands on the plates to generate a voltage reading.
actions: Place your hands down flatly on each plate
Reverse your connections with the plates and wires (if no reading)
Clean the plates with a pencil eraser or steel wool (if no reading)
